causes.label: Circuit breaker/fuse is tripped/blown
remedies: Check house circuit breakers/fuses.
Replace fuses or reset breaker.
Washer should have separate outlet.

causes.label: Electronics need to be reset
remedies: Unplug washer, wait 2 minutes, plug back in and press Start.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Electronics need to be reset"

causes.label: Start was not pressed
remedies: Press Start.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Start was not pressed"

causes.label: Lid magnet missing
remedies: Call for service.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Lid magnet missing"

causes.label: Shifting mechanism is disengaging the motor
remedies: When the machine is manually turned off, the shifter will disengage the motor before completely shutting down.
If lid is raised before the motor is disengaged, it will resume when lid is closed.
Make sure the spin cycle selected matches the load you are
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Shifting mechanism is disengaging the motor"

causes.label: Dye transfer
remedies: Sort whites or lightly colored items from dark colors Use more detergent (especially with larger loads).
Be sure to follow

symptoms.symptom: Grayed or yellowed clothes Lint or residue on clothes

causes.label: Water is not hot enough
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Water is not hot enough"

causes.label: Washer is overloaded
remedies: Select load size to match clothes load.
Add detergent as wash basket fills with water before you load
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Washer is overloaded"

causes.label: Incorrect sorting
remedies: Separate lint producers from lint collectors.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Incorrect sorting"

causes.label: Washing too long
remedies: Wash small loads for a shorter time than larger loads Add detergent as wash basket fills with water, before you load clothes.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Washing too long"

causes.label: Detergent not dissolving
remedies: Try a liquid detergent.
Use warmer water temperature.
Load clothes no higher than the top row of holes in the washer
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Detergent not dissolving"

causes.label: Incorrect use of fabric softener
remedies: Check fabric softener package for instructions and follow directions for using dispenser.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 15: "Incorrect use of fabric softener"

symptoms.symptom: Pilling Snags, holes, tears, rips or excessive wear Wrinkling “Metallic clicking” Back and forth

causes.label: Pins, snaps, hooks, sharp buttons, belt buckles, zippers and sharp objects left in pockets
remedies: Fasten snaps, hooks, buttons and zippers.
Remove loose items like pins, objects in pockets and sharp buttons.
Turn knits (which snag easily) inside out.
Check bleach package instructions for proper amount.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Pins, snaps, hooks, sharp buttons, belt buckles, zippers and sharp objects left in pockets"

causes.label: Undiluted chlorine bleach
remedies: Never add undiluted bleach to wash or allow clothes to come in contact with undiluted bleach.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Undiluted chlorine bleach"

causes.label: Chemicals like hair bleach or dye, permanent wave solution Improper sorting
remedies: Rinse items that may have chemicals on them before washing.
Avoid mixing heavy items (like work clothes) with light items (like blouses).
Try a fabric softener.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Chemicals like hair bleach or dye, permanent wave solution Improper sorting"

causes.label: Overloading or incorrect water level
remedies: Load your washer so clothes have enough room to move freely with water covering all of the clothes.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Overloading or incorrect water level"

causes.label: Shifter mechanism is engaging or disengaging
remedies: The drive system will engage at the start of agitate and disengage when agitate is complete.
This occurs multiple times during the wash.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Shifter mechanism is engaging or disengaging"

symptoms.symptom: Quick short agitation sounds at end of agitate

causes.label: Clothing redistribution
remedies: At the end of agitate, the motor makes short agitation strokes to redistribute the load.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Clothing redistribution"

causes.label: Relay switch
remedies: The relay makes a click sound when activated.
The water level activates the relay and stops filling.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Relay switch"

causes.label: Automatic Temperature Control Valve
remedies: This valve mixes in cold and hot water.
The “clicking” is the valve turning on and off.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Automatic Temperature Control Valve"

causes.label: Fuse is blown/circuit breaker is tripped
remedies: Check the house fuse/circuit breaker box and replace fuse or reset breaker.
Note: Most electric dryers use 2 fuses/breakers.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 17: "Fuse is blown/circuit breaker is tripped"

causes.label: Drying dirty items with clean ones
remedies: Use your dryer to dry only clean items.
Dirty items can stain clean items and the dryer.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 17: "Drying dirty items with clean ones"

symptoms.symptom: Clothes take too long to dry Clothes are wrinkled Clothes shrink

causes.label: Improper or obstructed ducting
remedies: Check to see if outside wall damper operates easily.
Check the Installation Instructions to make sure the dryer venting is correct.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 18: "Improper or obstructed ducting"

causes.label: Overdrying
remedies: Remove items while they still hold a slight amount of moisture.
Select a Less Dry setting.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 18: "Overdrying"

causes.label: Letting items sit in dryer after cycle ends
remedies: Remove items when cycle ends and fold or hang immediately.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 18: "Letting items sit in dryer after cycle ends"

causes.label: Overloading
remedies: Separate large loads into smaller ones.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 18: "Overloading"

remedies: To avoid shrinkage, follow garment care labels exactly.
Some items may be pressed back into shape after drying If you are concerned about shrinkage in a particular item, do not machine wash or tumble dry it.
